text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports worsening ankle swelling, orthopnea, and shortness of breath, which led to an ambulance transfer to the ER for heart failure.
- history of present illness: the patient was hospitalized for congestive heart failure after several days of ankle edema, inability to lie flat, and dyspnea, with blood pressure 200/90. Likely causes are dietary sodium (frequent salty potato chips) and uncontrolled hypertension, with possible missed doses of antihypertensives. Symptoms have improved with diuretic therapy and walking; no chest pain or sleep disturbance since discharge.
- physical examination: BP 128/72, temperature 98.7, heart rate 72, respirations 18, SpO2 96%. No jugular venous distention, 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (previously noted, stable), clear lungs bilaterally, trace lower extremity edema. Echocardiogram: preserved EF 55%, abnormal diastolic filling, mild-to-moderate mitral regurgitation.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: ankle swelling, shortness of breath when lying flat, dyspnea requiring the patient to sleep propped up, feeling unwell, and urinary frequency from diuretic use. No chest pain currently.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: bumetanide (Bumex) 2 mg once daily (continued); losartan (Cozaar) 100 mg daily (continued); amlodipine (Norvasc) 5 mg once daily (continued). Renal artery ultrasound ordered; additional labs ordered.
- follow-up instructions: weigh daily and call if weight gain is 3 lb in 2 days; monitor blood pressure at home and keep a log with diet notes; reduce salt intake; see a nutritionist; renal artery ultrasound and labs; return visit in 3 months.
